family.description: This domain, named as the SECRET domain, is found at the C-terminal end of Tumour necrosis factor receptor (CrmD) from the orthopoxvirus Ectromelia virus. This domain binds a subset of human and mouse CC, CXC and C chemokines. It is thought to be responsible for the anti-chemokine activity of CrmD. The SECRET domain monomer adopts a beta-sandwich fold, consisting of two parallel beta-sheets with five and six anti-parallel strands, and the connecting loops [[cite:PUB00151577]]. This domain is also found in other uncharacterised sequences from poxvirus, including Protein OPG192 and Protein C8 from Vaccinia virus.
family.name: Tumour necrosis factor receptor, SECRET domain
